ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $BC = 1$, $AB = 2$. A perpendicular line is drawn from a point $P$ on the diagonal $BD$ to intersect $AB$ at point $F$ and $CD$ at point $E$. Line $EG$ is drawn parallel to $BD$ from point $E$ and intersects $BC$ at point $G$. Lines $FG$ and $DF$ are drawn to intersect $BD$ at point $H$. Calculate the value of $ \frac{DE}{BG}$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\
since EF$\perp$AB,\\
it follows that $\angle AFE=90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABC=\angle AFE$,\\
thus EF$\parallel$BC,\\
since EG$\parallel$BD,\\
it follows that quadrilateral EPBG is a parallelogram,\\
thus EP=BG,\\
thus $\tan \angle EDP= \frac{EP}{DE} = \frac{BC}{CD} = \frac{1}{2}$,\\
thus $\frac{DE}{BG} = \boxed{2}$;

The figure also draws FG and DF, and marks H, but H does not need to be used when finding DE/BG. Coordinate reasoning: Take coordinates according to the image as A=(0,0), B=(2,0), C=(2,1), D=(0,1), because AB=2 and BC=1. E is on CD, and EF is perpendicular to AB, so E=(x,1), F=(x,0) can be set. Therefore DE=x. The slope of diagonal BD is (0-1)/(2-0)=-1/2. Since EG ∥ BD, the line passing through E=(x,1) and with slope -1/2 intersects BC, that is x=2. Substituting gives the intersection point height y=1-(2-x)/2=x/2, so G=(2,x/2). Thus BG=x/2. Therefore DE/BG=x/(x/2)=2.
